This BLA was referred to the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) for advice and presented on July 9, 2015.

recommendation.text: No numeric vote is reported in the review documents; the Summary Review reproduces the ODAC minutes, which state that the majority of the committee agreed the SQUIRE efficacy/safety results support a positive benefit:risk assessment for necitumumab in the proposed population.

quote.quote: The majority of the committee agreed that the efficacy and safety results of SQUIRE in squamous cell NSCLC support a positive benefit: risk assessment of necitumumab in combination with gemcitabine/cisplatin in the proposed population.

linkages.concern: ODAC members were concerned about the toxicity of hypomagnesemia and wanted clear guidance on managing it (the review also identifies cardiopulmonary arrest and hypomagnesemia as major serious risks).
linkages.change: A Boxed Warning for the serious risks of Cardiopulmonary Arrest and Hypomagnesemia was added to the product labeling.

concern_quote.quote: Committee members were concerned about the toxicity of hypomagnesemia and suggested clear guidance either in the labeling or educational resources on how to manage this in a clinical setting.

change_quote.quote: As recommended by the ODAC, a Boxed Warning was incorporated in product labeling to highlight the serious risks of Cardiopulmonary Arrest and Hypomagnesemia.

linkages.concern: Some committee members advised consideration of recommending against use in subgroups that appeared to gain little or no benefit, specifically patients over age 70 and those whose tumors do not express EGFR.
linkages.change: The Use in Specific Populations section of labeling added a description of the apparent lack of efficacy in exploratory subgroup analyses in elderly patients (OS hazard ratio in patients >=70 years was 1.03).

concern_quote.quote: Some committee members advised that consideration should be given to recommending against use in patient subgroups that appeared to gain little or no benefit from the anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody, such as patients over age 70 years and those whose tumors do not express EGF receptor proteins.

change_quote.quote: added a description of regarding apparent lack of efficacy in exploratory subgroup analyses in elderly patients (hazard ratio for overall survival in patients 70 years or older was 1.03 (95% CI: 0.75, 1.42))

summary: Portrazza (necitumumab, BLA125547) was referred to the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC), which met on July 9, 2015; the Summary Review reproduces the ODAC minutes but no numeric vote is recorded. The committee's majority supported a positive benefit:risk for the squamous-NSCLC population, and the review explicitly states that a Boxed Warning for Cardiopulmonary Arrest and Hypomagnesemia was incorporated 'As recommended by the ODAC.' Committee concern about little/no benefit in subgroups (patients >=70 and EGFR-non-expressing tumors) corresponds to added Use in Specific Populations labeling describing lack of efficacy in elderly patients, though that labeling change is not explicitly tied to the ODAC.
